```{python}
# | label: simulate-processes

from joblib import Parallel, delayed

num_sims = 1000
birth_rate = 0.005
death_rate = birth_rate - 0.004
time_span = 1500
seed = 42

print(f"🎲 Generate {num_sims} birth-death process simulations...")
print(f"   Birth rate: {birth_rate}")
print(f"   Death rate: {death_rate}")
print(f"   Time span: {time_span} years")
print("=" * 60)

# Run simulations in parallel using all available CPU cores
simulated_processes = Parallel(n_jobs=-1)(
    delayed(simulate_birth_death_process)(
        birth_rate=birth_rate,
        death_rate=death_rate,
        max_time=time_span,
        random_seed=seed + i,
    )
    for i in range(num_sims)
)

print(f"\n✅ Completed {len(simulated_processes)} simulations")
```

## Derivative of the log-likelihoods

We derive
$$
    \frac{dlP_n}{d\lambda} = \frac{\mu  \left(\mu -\mu  n+\lambda  (n-\mu  t+1)+\lambda ^2 t\right)+e^{t (\lambda -\mu )} (n (\lambda -\mu ) (\lambda  t (\lambda -\mu )-\mu )-\mu  (3 \lambda +\mu ))+\lambda  e^{2 t (\lambda -\mu )} (2 \mu +\lambda  t (\mu -\lambda ))}{\lambda  (\lambda -\mu ) \left(e^{t (\lambda -\mu )}-1\right) \left(\lambda  e^{t (\lambda -\mu )}-\mu \right)}
$$

$$
    \frac{dlP_n}{d\mu} = \frac{\lambda ^2 t e^{t (\lambda -\mu )} \left(e^{t (\lambda -\mu )}-n\right)-\lambda  \left(-(2 \mu  n t+n+3) e^{t (\lambda -\mu )}+n+(\mu  t+2) e^{2 t (\lambda -\mu )}+\mu  t+1\right)-\mu  \left((\mu  n t+n-1) e^{t (\lambda -\mu )}-n-\mu  t+1\right)}{(\lambda -\mu ) \left(e^{t (\lambda -\mu )}-1\right) \left(\lambda  e^{t (\lambda -\mu )}-\mu \right)}
$$

Derivation of the derivative of the ages
$$
    \frac{dlP(age)}{d\lambda}
    = \frac{
            (\lambda  t-1) e^{\mu  t+T (\lambda -\mu )}
            - (\lambda  t+\lambda  T-1) e^{\mu  t+2 T (\lambda -\mu )}
            - \mu  T e^{\lambda  t}
            + 2 \mu  T e^{\lambda  t+T (\lambda -\mu )}
        }{
            \left(e^{T (\lambda -\mu )}-1\right) \left(\lambda  e^{\mu  t+T (\lambda -\mu )}-\mu  e^{\lambda  t}\right)
        } \\
    \frac{dlP(age)}{d\mu} = \frac{\lambda  T e^{\mu  t+2 T (\lambda -\mu )}+e^{\lambda  t} (\mu  (-t)+\mu  T+1)+(\mu  t-2 \mu  T-1) e^{\lambda  t+T (\lambda -\mu )}}{\left(e^{T (\lambda -\mu )}-1\right) \left(\lambda  e^{\mu  t+T (\lambda -\mu )}-\mu  e^{\lambda  t}\right)}
$$

```{python}
# | eval: true
# | label: fit-individual-models

print(f"🔬 Fit birth-death models to {len(simulated_processes)} simulated processes...")
print("=" * 60)


# Define a function to fit a single model
def fit_single_model(ages, time_span):
    """Fit a single birth-death model to given ages."""
    if len(ages) == 0:
        return None
    try:
        model = fit_birth_death_processes(
            list_of_ages=[ages],
            observation_time=time_span,
            is_ordered=True,
            method="L-BFGS-B",
            initial_params=None,
            parallel=False,
        )
        return model
    except Exception as e:
        return None


# Fit models in parallel
fitted_models = Parallel(n_jobs=-1)(
    delayed(fit_single_model)(ages, time_span) for ages in list_of_ages
)

# Count successes and failures
successful_fits = sum(
    1 for m in fitted_models if m is not None and m.get("success", False)
)
failed_fits = len(fitted_models) - successful_fits

print(f"   Total models: {len(simulated_processes)}")
print(f"   Successful fits: {successful_fits}")
print(f"   Failed fits: {failed_fits}")
print(f"   Success rate: {(successful_fits / len(simulated_processes) * 100):.1f}%")
```

```{python}
# | label: summary-statistics

print("📊 Compute summary statistics...")

# Collect birth and death rates from fitted models
birth_rates = [
    m["birth_rate"] for m in fitted_models if m is not None and m.get("success", False)
]
death_rates = [
    m["death_rate"] for m in fitted_models if m is not None and m.get("success", False)
]

print(
    f"   Successfully extracted {len(birth_rates)} birth rates and {len(death_rates)} death rates"
)

summary_stats = {
    "Parameter": ["Birth Rate", "Death Rate"],
    "True Value": [birth_rate, death_rate],
    "Mean": [np.mean(birth_rates), np.mean(death_rates)],
    "Median": [np.median(birth_rates), np.median(death_rates)],
    "Std": [np.std(birth_rates), np.std(death_rates)],
    "Min": [np.min(birth_rates), np.min(death_rates)],
    "Max": [np.max(birth_rates), np.max(death_rates)],
    "25%": [np.percentile(birth_rates, 25), np.percentile(death_rates, 25)],
    "75%": [np.percentile(birth_rates, 75), np.percentile(death_rates, 75)],
}

stats_df = pd.DataFrame(summary_stats)
print("\n📈 Parameter Estimation Summary:")
print("=" * 60)
print(stats_df.to_string(index=False, float_format="%.6f"))
```

```{python}
# | label: plot-bd-inference

print("📈 Generate parameter estimation density plots...")

if len(birth_rates) > 1:
    birth_kde = gaussian_kde(birth_rates)
    x_birth = np.linspace(
        min(birth_rates), min([max(birth_rates), 10 * birth_rate]), 100
    )
    fig_birth = go.Figure()
    fig_birth.add_trace(
        go.Scatter(
            x=x_birth,
            y=birth_kde(x_birth),
            mode="lines",
            name="Density",
            line=dict(color=ptolqual[0]),
            showlegend=False,
        )
    )
    # Add vertical line for true birth_rate
    fig_birth.add_trace(
        go.Scatter(
            x=[birth_rate, birth_rate],
            y=[0, max(birth_kde(x_birth))],
            mode="lines",
            name="λ",
            line=dict(color=ptolqual[1], dash="dash"),
            showlegend=False,
        )
    )
    # Add annotation for λ above the density curve
    fig_birth.add_annotation(
        x=birth_rate,  # point annotation above the true-rate line
        y=max(birth_kde(x_birth)) * 1.05,  # place slightly above the density peak
        text="True λ",
        showarrow=True,
        arrowhead=2,
        ax=0,
        ay=-30,  # draw arrow from label down to the line
        xanchor="center",
        font=dict(color=ptolqual[1], size=11),
        bgcolor="rgba(255,255,255,0.75)",
    )
    # Place a small, unobtrusive legend inside the plot
    fig_birth.update_layout(showlegend=False)
    fig_birth = apply_professional_styling(
        fig_birth, None, r"$\hat{\lambda}$", "Density"
    )
    fig_birth = apply_tufte_axes(fig_birth)
    # Format axes: rate with 4 decimals, density baseline at zero
    fig_birth.update_xaxes(tickformat=".4f")
    fig_birth.update_yaxes(rangemode="tozero")
    fig_birth.show()

    # Save the figure
    save_figure(fig_birth, "mv_birth_rate_density_marg", width=192, height=110)
    save_figure(fig_birth, "mv_birth_rate_density", width=397, height=200)
else:
    print("   ⚠️  Not enough fitted models to plot birth rate density.")

if len(death_rates) > 1:
    death_kde = gaussian_kde(death_rates)
    x_death = np.linspace(
        min(death_rates), min([max(death_rates), 10 * death_rate]), 100
    )
    fig_death = go.Figure()
    fig_death.add_trace(
        go.Scatter(
            x=x_death,
            y=death_kde(x_death),
            mode="lines",
            name="Density",
            line=dict(color=ptolqual[0]),
            showlegend=False,
        )
    )
    # Add vertical line for true death_rate
    fig_death.add_trace(
        go.Scatter(
            x=[death_rate, death_rate],
            y=[0, max(death_kde(x_death))],
            mode="lines",
            name="μ",
            line=dict(color=ptolqual[1], dash="dash"),
            showlegend=False,
        )
    )
    # Add annotation for μ to the above of the density curve
    fig_death.add_annotation(
        x=death_rate,  # Position to the right of the line
        y=max(death_kde(x_death)) * 1.05,  # Near the top of the density
        text="True μ",
        showarrow=True,
        arrowhead=2,
        ax=0,
        ay=-30,  # draw arrow from label down to the line
        xanchor="center",
        font=dict(color=ptolqual[1], size=11),
        bgcolor="rgba(255,255,255,0.75)",
    )
    fig_death = apply_professional_styling(fig_death, None, r"$\hat{\mu}$", "Density")
    fig_death = apply_tufte_axes(fig_death)
    # Format axes: rate with 4 decimals, density baseline at zero
    fig_death.update_xaxes(tickformat=".4f")
    fig_death.update_yaxes(rangemode="tozero")
    fig_death.update_layout(showlegend=False)
    fig_death.show()

    # Save the figure
    save_figure(fig_death, "mv_death_rate_density_marg", width=192, height=100)
    save_figure(fig_death, "mv_death_rate_density", width=397, height=200)
else:
    print("   ⚠️  Not enough fitted models to plot death rate density.")
```

```{python}
# | label: joint-density-plot

print("\n🎯 Create 2D joint density plot...")

if len(birth_rates) > 1 and len(death_rates) > 1:
    xy = np.vstack([birth_rates, death_rates])
    kde = gaussian_kde(xy)
    x_grid = np.linspace(min(birth_rates), 2 * birth_rate, 100)
    y_grid = np.linspace(min(death_rates), 3 * death_rate, 100)
    X, Y = np.meshgrid(x_grid, y_grid)
    positions = np.vstack([X.ravel(), Y.ravel()])
    Z = kde(positions).reshape(X.shape)
    fig_joint = go.Figure(
        data=go.Contour(
            x=x_grid,
            y=y_grid,
            z=Z,
            colorscale="Viridis",
            contours=dict(showlabels=True),
            colorbar=dict(title="Density"),
        )
    )
    fig_joint.add_trace(
        go.Scatter(
            x=[birth_rate],
            y=[death_rate],
            mode="markers",
            marker=dict(color=ptolqual[1], size=8, symbol="circle"),
            name="True Value",
        )
    )
    fig_joint = apply_professional_styling(
        fig_joint,
        None,
        "Birth Rate",
        "Death Rate",
    )
    fig_joint = apply_tufte_axes(fig_joint)
    # Format axes for rates
    fig_joint.update_xaxes(tickformat=".4f")
    fig_joint.update_yaxes(tickformat=".4f")
    try:
        from inf_bp_texts.visualization.plotting import apply_tufte_legend

        fig_joint = apply_tufte_legend(fig_joint, position="top right")
    except Exception:
        fig_joint.update_layout(showlegend=True)
    fig_joint.show()

    # Save the figure
    save_figure(fig_joint, "mv_joint_density_rates_marg", width=192, height=150)
    save_figure(fig_joint, "mv_joint_density_rates", width=397, height=250)
else:
    print("   ⚠️  Not enough fitted models for joint density plot.")
```

```{python}
# | label: box-plots

import plotly.graph_objs as go

# Prepare data for box plot
box_data = [
    birth_rates,
    death_rates,
]

labels = ["MLE Birth Rates", "MLE Death Rates"]
true_values = [birth_rate, death_rate]
means = [np.mean(birth_rates), np.mean(death_rates)]
medians = [np.median(birth_rates), np.median(death_rates)]

# Create summary table
mse_birth = np.mean((np.array(birth_rates) - birth_rate) ** 2)
mse_death = np.mean((np.array(death_rates) - death_rate) ** 2)

box_summary = pd.DataFrame({
    "Parameter": ["Birth Rate (λ)", "Death Rate (μ)"],
    "True Value": true_values,
    "Mean": means,
    "Median": medians,
    "Std Dev": [np.std(birth_rates), np.std(death_rates)],
    "Q1 (25%)": [np.percentile(birth_rates, 25), np.percentile(death_rates, 25)],
    "Q3 (75%)": [np.percentile(birth_rates, 75), np.percentile(death_rates, 75)],
    "Min": [np.min(birth_rates), np.min(death_rates)],
    "Max": [np.max(birth_rates), np.max(death_rates)],
    "Bias": [np.mean(birth_rates) - birth_rate, np.mean(death_rates) - death_rate],
    "Rel. Bias (%)": [
        (np.mean(birth_rates) - birth_rate) / birth_rate * 100,
        (np.mean(death_rates) - death_rate) / death_rate * 100
    ],
    "MSE": [mse_birth, mse_death],
    "RMSE": [np.sqrt(mse_birth), np.sqrt(mse_death)]
})

print("\n📊 Parameter Estimation Box Plot Summary:")
print("=" * 80)
print(box_summary.to_string(index=False, float_format="%.6f"))

fig_box = go.Figure()

for i, data in enumerate(box_data):
    fig_box.add_trace(
        go.Box(
            y=data,
            name=labels[i],
            boxmean=True,
            boxpoints="outliers",
            marker_color=ptolqual[0],
        )
    )
    # Add true value
    fig_box.add_trace(
        go.Scatter(
            x=[labels[i]],
            y=[true_values[i]],
            mode="markers",
            marker=dict(color=ptolqual[1], size=8, symbol="circle"),
            name="True",
            showlegend=(i == 0),
        )
    )
    # Add sample mean
    fig_box.add_trace(
        go.Scatter(
            x=[labels[i]],
            y=[means[i]],
            mode="markers",
            marker=dict(color=ptolqual[2], size=10, symbol="circle"),
            name="Mean",
            showlegend=(i == 0),
        )
    )
    # Add sample median
    fig_box.add_trace(
        go.Scatter(
            x=[labels[i]],
            y=[medians[i]],
            mode="markers",
            marker=dict(color=ptolqual[3], size=10, symbol="square"),
            name="Median",
            showlegend=(i == 0),
        )
    )

fig_box = apply_professional_styling(
    fig_box, "Box Plot of Fitted Birth and Death Rates", "Parameter", "Rate"
)
fig_box = apply_tufte_axes(fig_box)
fig_box.update_yaxes(tickformat=".4f", rangemode="tozero")
# Override showlegend for box plot
try:
    from inf_bp_texts.visualization.plotting import apply_tufte_legend

    fig_box = apply_tufte_legend(fig_box, position="top right")
except Exception:
    fig_box.update_layout(showlegend=True)
fig_box.show()

# Save the figure
save_figure(fig_box, "mv_parameter_boxplots", width=397, height=250)
```

```{python}
# | label: cumulative mult-proc
# | eval: false
cumulative_estimates = []
has_age = False

for i in [0, 1, int(num_sims / 8), int(num_sims / 4), int(num_sims / 2), int(num_sims)]:
    if not has_age:
        if len(list_of_ages[i]) > 1:
            has_age = True
    if has_age:
        model = fit_birth_death_processes(
            list_of_ages=list_of_ages[0 : (i + 1)],
            observation_time=time_span,
            is_ordered=True,
            initial_params=cumulative_estimates[-1] if (not i==0) None else,
            parallel=True,
        )
        cumulative_estimates.append(model.x)
    else:
        cumulative_estimates.append(None)

print(cumulative_estimates)
```
